title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional quarter-end capping check effective at the open of 2027-12-31 (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2027-12-28 close), the quarter whose drift window is the longest the family has measured
source: EST: owner-published standing rule, both governing documents re-fetched and re-extracted first-hand this session rather than inherited from the proposal or from any of the five sibling ledgers. FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-09 — the identical byte and stream counts four siblings recorded, so this is provably the same edition): section 4.8.6 gives every Russell US Style row frequency "Monthly", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45", price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month" carrying footnote 3; the "Quarterly / Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec" wording was read at the row level and belongs to the FTSE Emerging ex China RIC 22.5/45 rows, reproducing the December-2026 sibling's correction for a third time from an independent extraction. FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions — Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (same host, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 streams, re-fetched 2026-09-09): its schedule table's four capping rows were read at the column level and reproduce verbatim across all four 2026 quarters — style capping cut-off 11 March / 17 June / 9 September / 2 December, review effective open 23 March / 29 June / 21 September / 14 December, quarter-end cut-off 26 March / 25 June / 25 September / 28 December, quarter-end effective open 31 March / 30 June / 30 September / 31 December. THE 2027 DATES ARE RULE-DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED (the FAQ's dated table carries 2026 rows only), AND THE DERIVATION WAS TESTED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Quarter-end cut-off: the FAQ's own words are "closing prices from three trading days prior to the last business day of the quarter", the last business day of December 2027 is Friday 2027-12-31, and T-3 steps over Christmas Day observed on Friday 2027-12-24 — read this session from NYSE's own Holidays and Trading Hours page (nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-09), whose 2027 column reads "Friday, December 24 (Christmas Day observed)" and whose footnote reads "Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Years Day holiday is observed", keeping 2027-12-31 a full session — landing on Tuesday 2027-12-28. Review dates: review effective open = the Monday after the quarter's own implementation Friday, and the style capping cut-off = that Monday minus 12 calendar days. That pair reproduces ALL FOUR published 2026 columns to the day, and each cut-off it produces is a Wednesday, as all four published ones are. December's implementation Friday is fixed by a THIRD primary — FTSE Russell ground rules v7.2 section 4.2.3, "Reconstitution occurs on the fourth Friday in June and the second Friday in December", quoted in russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11.json from that lane's own fetch — so December 2027's is Friday 2027-12-10 (the month's Fridays are 3, 10, 17, 24, 31), review effective open Monday 2027-12-13, style capping cut-off Wednesday 2027-12-01. Filed estimate on the four counts this family always records: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, the confirmed-tier prefixes in market-events-data.ts have no member for an index owner's own published methodology, the FAQ's schedule table carries "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes.", and the two owner documents still disagree about the check's frequency (guide "Monthly", FAQ "conducted quarterly", both re-read verbatim this session). Conditional by construction — the FAQ says "If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Canonical file written by this event's own initial research after reading in full the single proposal carrying this id, checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), which read proposals/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-12-31.from-sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31.json in full first, then re-fetched every owner document rather than inheriting its readings. Ledger: docs/research/events/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-12-31.md. THE PROPOSAL HANDED FORWARD EXACTLY ONE QUESTION AND IT IS NOW SETTLED. It declined to derive the quarterly review dates because December 2026's implementation Friday is the SECOND Friday where March and September use the third, and it would not extend an inconsistent-looking pattern by hand. The pattern is not inconsistent: the ordinal is not part of the rule. The rule is the Monday after EACH QUARTER'S OWN implementation Friday, which the ground rules define separately per quarter — fourth Friday in June, second Friday in December, and the quarterly IPO review's third Friday in March and September. Under that reading all four published 2026 columns reproduce to the day, every derived cut-off is a Wednesday exactly as all four published ones are, and an independent lane's entry corroborates the Monday half (russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2027-03-22 is the Monday after the third Friday of March 2027). December 2027 therefore reads style capping cut-off Wednesday 2027-12-01, review effective open Monday 2027-12-13, quarter-end test struck on the Tuesday 2027-12-28 close, effective open Friday 2027-12-31. THE HEADLINE IS WHAT THAT GEOMETRY IS WORTH: the cut-off-to-test drift window is 18 trading sessions, the LONGEST this family has measured — against 17 for December 2026, 13 for the untracked September 2027 instance and 11 for March 2027 — and every one of the 18 is a FULL session, where December 2026's 17 contained a 1:00 p.m. half day on 2026-12-24 (src/domain/market-calendar.ts), so in trading hours the gap is nearer 9% than 6%. The extra session comes from the front of the window, not the back: December 2027's recon Friday falls on the 10th against 2026's 11th, moving the review effective open to 12-13 and the cut-off to 12-01, while T-3 lands on 12-28 in both years. Re-based on 1,254 daily bars (2021-09-09 to 2026-09-08, Yahoo, fetched this session), a 45%-reset cohort clears the 48% trigger in 105 of 1,236 rolling 18-session windows = 8.50%, against 96/1,237 = 7.76% at 17 sessions and 40/1,243 = 3.22% at 11. THIS SESSION'S ARITHMETIC IS THE FIFTH INDEPENDENT REBUILD AND IT REPRODUCES THE FAMILY EXACTLY: run against the siblings' own window lengths it returns 40/1,243 = 3.22% (the March sibling's count to the window), 49/1,242 = 3.95% and 96/1,237 = 7.76% (the December sibling's counts to the window), which is evidence toward that sibling's FT-1 that the re-based implementation is the correct one — recorded here, not scored, because scoring another event's forward test is not this lane's to do. A CROSS-FAMILY CONVERGENCE WORTH RECORDING AND NOT OVER-READING: the proposer, sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31, independently found December 2027 gives ITS family the longest drift window of its four quarters too. The two findings share a date and not a cause — the Select Sector one turns on Christmas 2027 falling on a Saturday and removing every early close, this one turns on the recon Friday landing a day earlier in the month. Both still land on stand aside, which is the honest reading of a coincidence. SCOPE AND SIZE RE-VERIFIED FROM THE VENDOR THIS SESSION, NOT INHERITED: the iShares product screener returns IWF $125.57B, IWD $83.37B, IWP $19.58B, IWY $15.83B, IWS $15.52B, IWO $14.68B, IWN $14.48B, IWX $3.92B = $292.95B. IWY's over-4.8% company cohort (Alphabet's two lines combined per the guide's own company rule) reads 46.81% and IWF's 44.47% on holdings dated 2026-08-27; the single-name leg is dead by a wide margin (NVDA 16.21% in IWY against a 22.5% cap and a 24% trigger); a fired recap moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.83B, roughly $475M, across five mega caps. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the family's measured grounds, re-verified this session: docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped for rebalanc|reconstitution|russell|capping|index.flow|IWF|IWY -> zero hits in both, so no house playbook is index-flow-keyed, and an ETF proxy in symbols would make the deterministic screen trip on mega-cap beta rather than on anything about this rule. THE CORRIDOR IS FIVE TRACKED EVENTS, the thinnest this family has seen: fhfa-hpi-2027-12-28 (the corridor's only confirmed entry) shares the test's own price date; fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 (medium) lands mid-window; and 2027-12-31 itself carries sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31 (the S&P conditional twin, clearing after the close where this one clears at the open), sifma-bond-early-close-2027-12-31 and fed-board-closure-2027-12-31 — so a forced print lands into a half-staffed tape, an execution note and not a trade. TWO DATED ADJACENTS PROPOSED IN THE SAME PR: russell-reconstitution-2027-12-10 (the December semi-annual reconstitution, which IS this test's reset and is the one upstream date this calendar does not track) and russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-09-30 (the immediately preceding instance of this family, the gap the proposal named and declined as outside its corridor).
